insights.takeaway: A new ₹10,000 crore 'SME Growth Fund' and a ₹2,000 crore top-up for the 'Self-Reliant India Fund' have been introduced for MSMEs.
insights.quote: A new 'SME Growth Fund' worth ₹10,000 crore has been introduced for SMEs.

insights.takeaway: SMEs invoicing Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) must now use the TReDS platform for invoice discounting, ensuring timely payments.
insights.quote: Whenever the SMEs raise an invoice to the CPSE... it will be done through the TReDS platform.

insights.takeaway: A new, simplified Income Tax Act (2025) with easier rules and forms will be effective from April 1, 2026, simplifying individual tax compliance.
insights.quote: The new Income Tax Act (2025) will be levied from 1st April 2026.

insights.takeaway: A six-month 'One Time Foreign Asset Disclosure Scheme' is introduced to help individuals regularize undeclared foreign assets, avoiding penalties.
insights.quote: The government has introduced a 'One Time Foreign Asset Disclosure Scheme'.

insights.takeaway: Tax Collected at Source (TCS) for foreign travel packages and remittances for education or medical payments abroad has been reduced from 5% to 2%.
insights.quote: The rate was currently at 5%, and the government has now reduced it to 2%.

insights.takeaway: Securities Transaction Tax (STT) on Futures has increased from 0.02% to 0.05%, and on Options from 0.1% to 0.125%, impacting derivative traders.
insights.quote: The STT on Futures has now been increased from 0.02% to 0.05%.

insights.takeaway: Capital gains exemption on Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGBs) now only applies if purchased directly from and redeemed with RBI, not from the open market.
Income from share buybacks, previously taxed as 'Income from Other Source', will now be taxed as 'Capital Gains', potentially offering tax savings.
insights.quote: These were currently treated as 'Income from Other Source'... But these will be taxed as per 'Capital Gains'.

insights.takeaway: The Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming, and Comics (AVGC) industry is projected to create two million jobs, with government support through 'Content Creator Labs'.
insights.quote: AVGC... There is a possibility of two million jobs to be created.

insights.takeaway: Installing an oversized solar plant is often uneconomical if DISCOM buyback rates are low and unused electricity credits lapse annually on March 31st.
insights.quote: How much does DISCOM pay you? It pays you ₹3.26... On March 31st, the applicable bill in minus will lapse.

insights.takeaway: Be aware that solar panels come in A, B, and C grades; lower-grade panels with defects might be used by some vendors, affecting long-term performance.
insights.quote: There are A grade, B grade, C grade... 20 panels, among them might have minor defects.

insights.takeaway: A solar inverter can often operate at 125-130% of its rated capacity, potentially allowing a smaller, cheaper inverter for a slightly larger plant.
insights.quote: The Sungrow inverter operates at a capacity of 125% to 130%.

insights.takeaway: For long-lasting solar structures, ensure they are prefabricated, anti-cyclonic, galvanised, and that all holes are pre-drilled before coating to prevent rust.
insights.quote: Solar panels can last that long. But we cannot say the same thing about this structure... The holes must be done prior to the galvanizing process.

insights.takeaway: Central and state government subsidies significantly reduce solar plant costs, and reputable vendors can manage the entire subsidy and net meter application process.
insights.quote: ₹78,000 subsidy from the central government... their team handled the application process on my behalf.

insights.takeaway: Some solar vendors offer a "good zero guarantee," compensating you if the solar plant generates less than a promised minimum electricity, mitigating performance risk.
insights.quote: If less electricity is generated, then difference amount will be paid by Solar Square.

insights.takeaway: When calculating solar ROI, accurately factor in annual panel degradation (e.g., 0.7%) and an assumed annual electricity bill inflation (e.g., 3%) over 25 years.
insights.quote: We have considered the annual degradation as respectable 0.7%... this electricity bill will inflate by 3% every year.

insights.takeaway: NPS offers a significant tax deduction (80CCD) up to ₹7.5 lakhs, even in the new tax regime, potentially saving ₹2.5 lakhs annually for high earners.
insights.quote: There is only one deduction left, i.e. 80 CCD. which is available to NPS and PPF subscribers.

insights.takeaway: NPS now allows up to 100% equity exposure in new schemes, similar to mutual funds, removing the previous 75% cap for younger investors seeking higher growth.
insights.quote: in the new schemes, upto 100% equity exposure, just like mutual funds has been allowed.

insights.takeaway: The NPS lock-in period has been significantly reduced to 15 years or until age 60, whichever is earlier, offering much greater liquidity than before.
insights.quote: The rule has now been changed to either 15 years or until the age of 60.

insights.takeaway: NPS now allows 100% withdrawal for corpus up to ₹8 lakhs. For larger amounts, you can withdraw 80% as a lumpsum and only 20% for annuity, improving flexibility.
insights.quote: The former 60:40 rule has now been changed to 80:20.

insights.takeaway: NPS now permits four partial withdrawals (up to 25% of own contribution) during the tenure, up from three, and also introduces an option to take loans against your contribution.
insights.quote: now it has now been increased to four withdrawals... But now an option has been given... to opt for loans.

insights.takeaway: Senior citizens can now invest gratuity or excess funds in NPS, potentially achieving 100% equity returns. Nominees receive the full amount tax-free upon death.
insights.quote: After retirement, many people can park their excess money in NPS... nominee will receive this money, without any taxation.

insights.takeaway: Corporate NPS subscribers can now get tax exemption up to 14% of Basic + DA (previously 10%), allowing deductions up to ₹7.5 lakhs under 80CCD(2) in the new tax regime.
insights.quote: Earlier, its limit was increased to 10% of Basic + DA. It has now been increased to 14% of Basic + DA.

insights.takeaway: Indians renouncing citizenship and settling abroad can now withdraw 100% of their NPS corpus without any rules or regulations.
insights.quote: As soon as they've renounced their citizenship... You are then allowed to withdraw 100% NPS.

insights.takeaway: On long-term loans, you pay significantly more interest than principal, and your principal balance reduces very slowly in the initial years of repayment.
insights.quote: you will be paying me more than ₹65 lakhs in interest.

insights.takeaway: Always choose a 'reducing balance interest rate' over a 'flat interest rate' as flat rates cost significantly more, even if they appear lower.
insights.quote: 10% 'flat interest rate'... is worse than 17% 'reducing balance interest rate'.

insights.takeaway: Banks often increase loan interest rates immediately when the repo rate rises but require you to apply to reduce them when it falls. Regularly check your statements.
insights.quote: when the interest rate increases, then the banks immediately increase the home loan. But when it reduces, then you have to apply and reduce it.

insights.takeaway: Paying just one extra EMI per year can significantly reduce your total interest paid and shorten your loan tenure by several years.
insights.quote: If you start paying an additional EMI... I saved an interest of ₹5 lakhs.

insights.takeaway: When taking a new loan, opt for EBLR (External Benchmark Linked Rate) over MCLR (Marginal Cost of Funds Based Lending Rate) as EBLR is more transparent and linked to the repo rate.
insights.quote: you must take the EBLR.

insights.takeaway: Be aware of various loan charges. Always demand a Key Fact Statement (KFS) to understand all costs and the true Annualised Percentage Rate (APR) of your loan.
insights.quote: Always demand a KFS, i.e. 'Key Fact Statement'.

insights.takeaway: Lenders assess your credit score, Fixed Obligation to Income Ratio (FOIR, ideally below 40%), and Debt to Income ratio to determine your loan eligibility.
insights.quote: FOIR stands for 'Fixed Obligation to Income Ratio'.

insights.takeaway: After fully repaying your loan, always obtain a 'No Due Certificate' (NDC) from the bank to confirm your loan is officially closed and prevent future disputes.
insights.quote: definitely get the most important document from the bank.. i.e. 'No Due Certificate'.

insights.takeaway: To claim HRA over ₹1 lakh, provide your landlord's PAN. A rent agreement is now mandatory for all HRA claims, and you must declare if paying rent to relatives.
insights.quote: If you are claiming more than ₹1 lakh HRA... you will have to mandatorily provide landlord's PAN.

insights.takeaway: Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune, and Ahmedabad are now considered metro cities for HRA exemption, allowing employees in these areas to claim higher HRA benefits.
insights.quote: Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune, Ahmedabad... employees from these cities will be able to take benefit of higher HRA.

insights.takeaway: The old tax regime now offers significantly higher exemptions for education (₹3000/child/month), hostel (₹9000/child/month), meal coupons (₹200/meal), and gifts (up to ₹15,000).
insights.quote: Education allowance will go upto ₹72,000/ year. Hostel allowance upto ₹2,16,000/ year.

insights.takeaway: With new, higher exemptions, the old tax regime is now more beneficial for those with a rented house, children, or a home loan. Re-evaluate your tax regime choice.
Salaried employees can pay zero tax up to ₹12.75 lakhs in the new tax regime, thanks to the ₹60,000 87A rebate and ₹75,000 standard deduction.
insights.quote: Salaried employees won't pay tax upto ₹12,75,000 in the new tax regime.

insights.takeaway: ITR deadlines for traders (ITR 3) and presumptive taxation filers (ITR 4) have been extended by one month. The deadline to revise returns is also extended.
insights.quote: Traders and presumptive taxation filers will receive relaxation for a month.

insights.takeaway: The previous Financial Year (FY) and Assessment Year (AY) terminology has been replaced by a single term: 'Tax Year', simplifying annual tax period references.
insights.quote: Only one name has been kept this year... i.e. Tax Year.

insights.takeaway: Secure significant car discounts by combining credit card rewards for down payments with direct dealer negotiations, especially on slow-moving models.
insights.quote: I got three different types of discounts on it.

insights.takeaway: Maximize your savings by choosing banks offering high interest rates, like those linked to the repo rate, and utilize UPI cards for cashback on daily spending.
insights.quote: you will get 100% repo rate as interest.

insights.takeaway: For large purchases like cars, prioritize credit cards offering milestone-based bonus reward points, as these significantly boost your earnings beyond base rewards.
insights.quote: You've to select those cards in which you'll get 'Milestone Based Bonus Reward Points'.

insights.takeaway: When making large credit card payments at dealerships, always negotiate the Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) to reduce the extra charge passed on to you.
insights.quote: But you can negotiate this MDR.

insights.takeaway: Achieve the highest value from credit card reward points by transferring them to airline or hotel loyalty programs, often yielding better returns than direct redemption.
insights.quote: You will only get the best value.. when you transfer these points to an airline or a hotel programme.

insights.takeaway: When using credit cards for large payments, ensure sufficient credit limit, pay immediately to avoid CIBIL impact, and verify the merchant's category code for reward eligibility.
insights.quote: There are certain risks in this, which you must be aware of.

insights.takeaway: Seek direct dealer discounts on slow-selling car models. If a loan is a condition for a discount, take the minimum possible amount to qualify.
insights.quote: Suzuki started giving heavy discounts on it. Firstly, I straightaway received a discount of ₹1 lakh.

insights.takeaway: The 18% GST on life and health insurance premiums will be removed for payments made after September 22, 2025. No refunds for advance payments.
insights.quote: If you pay the premiums of any of these policies after 22nd September, 2025. then GST won't be levied.

insights.takeaway: Existing life and health insurance policyholders will see their premiums become roughly 15% cheaper after the 18% GST removal.
insights.quote: The premium generated on your life or health insurance, after 22nd September. It will be roughly 15% lesser.

insights.takeaway: New policyholders can currently avail significant discounts, up to 20% on Term Insurance premiums, beyond the upcoming GST benefit, for a limited time.
insights.quote: You will receive up to a 20% discount on Term Insurance premiums.

insights.takeaway: Unlike term insurance, whose premium is fixed for life, health insurance premiums typically increase with your age over time.
insights.quote: Even after purchasing health insurance, it's premiums keep increasing with your age. Unlike term insurance, whose premium is fixed.

insights.takeaway: Insurance companies losing Input Tax Credit due to GST removal will face 18% higher costs, which will likely lead to increased premiums in the future.
insights.quote: If you don't receive input tax credit, then the company's cost will increase by 18%.

insights.takeaway: The GST deduction primarily benefits pure risk policies like term and health insurance, rather than investment-linked plans such as Money Back or ULIPs.
insights.quote: The biggest advantage of GST deduction will reflect in term and health insurance policies. Because these are pure risk policies.

insights.takeaway: Purchase term insurance today to lock in the cheapest premium for your lifetime, as future premiums are expected to rise due to increasing company costs.
insights.quote: My suggestion for you is to purchase term insurance.. and lock the cheapest premium today. Because they will be same for your lifetime.

insights.takeaway: Offer letters are not legally binding; insist on a signed employment contract with all terms and keep a copy for legal protection.
insights.quote: Offer Letter is NOT a legal document.

insights.takeaway: Non-compete clauses are generally not legally enforceable in India if they restrict your fundamental right to earn a livelihood.
insights.quote: this non-compete clause, leaving certain special circumstances, will not be considered valid in court.

insights.takeaway: Employment bonds for arbitrary amounts or without actual training are often invalid; never sign a blank cheque for a bond.
insights.quote: If the company collects a bond cheque signed by you... Definitely don't do this.

insights.takeaway: Maximize savings interest by using accounts like Slice that offer RBI repo rate (5.25%) compounded daily, or 7.75% on 1.5-year FDs.
insights.quote: Slice... gives a great interest on the money left in your savings account... equivalent to the RBI's repo rate.

insights.takeaway: Negotiate for a higher fixed pay component and lower variable pay, as variable pay can be 0-100% and tied to unachievable targets.
insights.quote: If the variable pay is high it means that you are giving too much power to the company.

insights.takeaway: Non-managerial employees working over 48 hours weekly are entitled to overtime pay at twice their basic salary rate, effective November 2025.
insights.quote: the employer has to pay overtime for the additional hours to their employees. That too, twice the rate of your basic salary.

insights.takeaway: Always obtain Form 16 from your employer to verify that your Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) has been deposited with the Income Tax department.
insights.quote: Hence, always keep Form 16 with you. Always remember to ask Form 16 from your employer.

insights.takeaway: You are eligible for gratuity after five years of service; fixed-term employees qualify proportionally after just one year under new labour codes.
insights.quote: If you are in a fixed-term employment... Even then you will be eligible for gratuity after one year of service.

insights.takeaway: Always obtain a relieving letter from your previous employer; it's crucial proof that your contract has ended and prevents PF transfer issues.
insights.quote: That proof is known to be your 'relieving letter'.

insights.takeaway: Understand the difference between tax exemptions (reduce taxable income) and deductions (reduce net taxable income) for effective tax planning.
insights.quote: EARNING - EXEMPTIONS = TAXABLE INCOME. and, TAXABLE INCOME - DEDUCTIONS = NET TAXABLE INCOME.

insights.takeaway: When choosing a tax regime, compare post-tax returns. An 8% tax-exempt PPF return can equal a 12-13% return from other funds in the old regime.
insights.quote: 8% return in PPF is approximately equal to 12%-13% return in equity or debt mutual fund.

insights.takeaway: Optimize your HRA exemption by strategically adjusting your basic salary component; there's an ideal balance for maximum tax savings based on your rent.
insights.quote: For every rent there is an optimized number you can keep for HRA to save maximum tax.

insights.takeaway: Utilize Leave Travel Allowance (LTA) for family travel expenses (train, flight) for up to two trips in four years, if offered by your company.
insights.quote: Your travel expenses for train, flight, etc., can be exempted under Leave Travel Allowance (LTA).

insights.takeaway: Claim reimbursements for office-related expenses like mobile, internet bills, or food coupons (e.g., Sodexo for Rs 31,200 annually) to save tax.
insights.quote: Try to claim such small expenses made on behalf of the company as reimbursements rather than as allowances.

insights.takeaway: Salaried employees should always claim the Rs 50,000 Standard Deduction, as it automatically reduces your taxable income.
insights.quote: Salaried employees can firstly opt for Rs 50,000 standard deduction, which is a no-brainer.

insights.takeaway: Exercise caution with NPS (80CCD) due to high lock-in and low annuity returns. Only opt for it if essential to reduce taxable income below a slab.
insights.quote: I don't suggest it a lot since the lock-in period is high. Upon retirement, you have to buy minimum 40% annuity.

insights.takeaway: Claim health insurance premiums under 80D (up to Rs 25,000 for self/family, Rs 50,000 for parents) and Rs 5,000 for preventive health check-ups.
insights.quote: Under health insurance, you can claim maximum upto Rs 25,000 personally and Rs 50,000 for parents.

insights.takeaway: Do not take loans like home or electric vehicle loans solely for tax benefits; only opt for them if genuinely necessary.
insights.quote: Now, do not forcefully take such loans to save tax.

insights.takeaway: Avoid insurance plans that combine investment and insurance, as they typically offer inadequate life cover and poor investment returns.
insights.quote: This is Insurance + Investment

insights.takeaway: High commissions (up to 25%) motivate agents to sell combo insurance plans, even if these products are not beneficial for customers.
insights.quote: Agents get high commissions up to 25% when they sell these plans

insights.takeaway: Combo insurance plans provide insufficient life cover; for example, a Rs 50,000 annual premium might only yield a Rs 6.5 lakh sum assured, far below recommended levels.
insights.quote: My sum assured is 6.5 lakh if I pay 50,000 Rupees premium annually

insights.takeaway: The investment component of combo insurance plans offers extremely low Internal Rate of Return (IRR), often around 5-6%, which is typically worse than fixed deposits and fails to beat inflation.
insights.quote: your money will grow with a rate of only 5% in this plan

insights.takeaway: Surrendering combo insurance plans prematurely results in substantial financial losses; you might lose over half of your total premiums paid.
insights.quote: I will get only 85K Rupees if I surrender it today. It means I have to face a loss of 1.15 Lakh

insights.takeaway: Bonuses declared in combo insurance policies are often paid only at maturity, years after declaration, significantly reducing their real value due to inflation.
insights.quote: That bonus will be in your policy and you will get it on maturity after 10 more years

insights.takeaway: Investing in low-return combo insurance plans for years leads to massive opportunity costs; the same money invested in good mutual funds could yield significantly higher wealth.
insights.quote: You are in an 18.5 Lakh loss if you are invested in these plans for only 10 years

insights.takeaway: Build financial security by prioritizing term insurance, health insurance, an emergency fund (6 months' salary), and then diversified investments in stocks, mutual funds, and debt.
insights.quote: Your priority should be to take term insurance for yourself

insights.takeaway: Always conduct your own research and verify financial advice, even from trusted relatives or agents, as their incentives might not align with your best interests.
insights.quote: I request you that don't trust blindly on anyone including me

insights.takeaway: Be cautious about financial advice from influencers, especially those promoting unregulated trading apps, as their incentives often conflict with viewers' financial well-being.
insights.quote: financial advice should not be taken from everyone.

insights.takeaway: Organize your favorite stocks into up to five watchlists on Zerodha Kite, each holding 50 stocks, for quick and efficient access.
insights.quote: You have 5 lists so you can add different stocks as you wish

insights.takeaway: In Zerodha Kite, "Holdings" are for shares held overnight (delivery), while "Positions" are for stocks bought and sold within the same trading day (intraday).
insights.quote: Holdings mean your equity deliveries. If you hold more than a day, then it comes in holdings

insights.takeaway: Use CNC (Cash N Carry) for holding shares longer than a day (delivery) and MIS (Margin Intraday Square Off) for buying and selling stocks within the same trading day.
insights.quote: CNC means CASH N CARRY. We choose this option when we want to hold shares for more than a day (Delivery)

insights.takeaway: A Market order executes at the current market price. A Limit order allows you to set a desired price, but it will only execute if that price is met.
insights.quote: MARKET always means the price which is being traded in the market... LIMIT always means that stock will be bought/sold at your desired price

insights.takeaway: Use Stop Loss Limit (SL) or Stop Loss Market (SLM) orders to protect against significant losses. These orders automatically sell your shares when a set trigger price is reached.
insights.quote: STOP LOSS LIMIT and STOP LOSS MARKET are the orders which protect you from a loss

insights.takeaway: Bracket Orders (BO) let you set a target profit, a stop loss, and a trailing stop loss simultaneously for intraday trades, managing both risk and reward.
insights.quote: In bracket order, you can set a stop loss And you can also set a cap on your profit also

insights.takeaway: Use After Market Orders (AMO) to place buy or sell orders even when the market is closed. These orders will be executed on the next trading day.
insights.quote: You can put order even after market hours and it will be executed the next day

insights.takeaway: GTT (Good Till Triggered) orders remain valid for one year, allowing you to set specific buy or sell price triggers for long-term investing without daily market tracking.
insights.quote: GTT means this order will be valid for 1 year and you can place 50 orders like this

insights.takeaway: Be aware that GTT orders can be canceled if the stock undergoes a split or if the trigger price is met but the final buy/sell price is not achieved.
insights.quote: Suppose ONGC split its stock Then the 1 share of 78 may be changed in 2 shares of 39 Then your all entries... will be considered invalid and your GTT order will be canceled.

insights.takeaway: Avoid unnecessary credit or small loans. Only take significant loans for assets like a house, car, or business if you have a clear repayment plan based on your income.
insights.quote: That's why take a loan only when you desperately need it.

insights.takeaway: Maintain proper accounts to track your expenses. This helps identify where your money truly goes, allowing you to make informed decisions and reduce unnecessary spending.
insights.quote: So if you maintain your accounts properly and tally it in month end, You will be able to analyze, head-wise expenses and save a lot.

insights.takeaway: Quitting bad habits like smoking or excessive drinking can save significant money over time. Investing these daily savings can lead to substantial wealth growth and improve your health.
insights.quote: If you save 50 rs a day, how much you will save in a month? You will save 1500 in a month, in a year? 18,000/-

insights.takeaway: Maintain meticulous records of important documents like insurance policies, warranty cards, and PF details. This prevents late penalties, lost benefits, and unnecessary expenses.
insights.quote: You will proper record keeping will benefit immensely in long run.

insights.takeaway: Simply saving money isn't enough; you must invest it to combat inflation. Choose investment options that suit you, ensuring your money grows over time rather than losing value.
insights.quote: The money in bank, piggy bank or at home is not safe, Inflation eats it, Reduces it's value, That's why you not only have to save your money But also invest it.

insights.takeaway: Understand your household's consumption patterns for daily consumables. Buying these items in bulk can significantly reduce costs compared to purchasing small packs regularly.
insights.quote: Higher the quantity, lower the price! So if you know your consumption, stop buying small packs and buy in bulk.

insights.takeaway: Prioritize and invest in your health, even if it means spending on gym memberships or activities. Good health is crucial for earning capacity and enjoying your wealth in the long term.
insights.quote: IF your body does not support how will you earn ? And even if you earn somehow, what's the point if you can not utilize it / enjoy it?

insights.takeaway: Continuously learn new skills and adapt to technological changes. This ensures you remain relevant in the job market, opens new opportunities, and provides alternative income streams.
insights.quote: In this challenging environment only those will thrive, who will continue to learn.

insights.takeaway: Salaried individuals with income from one house property, interest/dividend, and small agricultural income can file ITR 1.
insights.quote: If these 3 Heads i.e Income from Salary, Income from One House Property and Income from Other Sources If you have that Then you can file ITR 1

insights.takeaway: Do not file ITR 1 if you are a company director, hold unlisted shares or foreign assets, have capital gains, or wish to carry forward losses.
insights.quote: Who cannot file ITR 1 If someone is a Director in the company If they have unlisted shares i.e If they have ESOPs Or If they have an Asset beyond India

insights.takeaway: Use Form 16 from your employer, Form 26AS for TDS details, and the Annual Information Statement (AIS) to accurately file your ITR.
insights.quote: For this, you will have to see 2 simple forms 1st Form is Form 16 2nd Form is Form 26AS

insights.takeaway: If your employer missed some income or deductions, you can rectify these details while filing your Income Tax Return (ITR) to ensure accuracy.
insights.quote: This amount can become more or less Which while filing ITR you can rectify.

insights.takeaway: When claiming exemptions or deductions in your ITR, ensure you have proper proof for each claim to avoid issues with tax authorities.
insights.quote: If you are adamant You want to declare some exemptions here Then you do it But you need to have proper proof of that

insights.takeaway: Tax planning is a continuous process from April 1st to March 31st; ITR filing is done closer to the deadline and cannot include new planning.
insights.quote: Tax Planning starts from 1st April and ends on 31st March After that, you cannot do any Planning.

insights.takeaway: Declare additional income like freelancing or rental income to your employer; this helps avoid interest penalties for late advance tax payments.
insights.quote: There won't be any interest penalty levied on you For paying Late Tax

insights.takeaway: Submit all deduction proofs (e.g., ELSS, Mediclaim) to your employer by November-December to prevent excess TDS and avoid opportunity loss on refunds.
insights.quote: you definitely submit to the employer So that it gets updated in Form 16

insights.takeaway: The e-Shram card is a government initiative to create a national database for unorganized sector workers, enabling direct benefit transfers and access to social security schemes.
insights.quote: The initiative of the e-Shram Card, has introduced by the Ministry of Labour and Employment.

insights.takeaway: To register for an e-Shram card, you must be aged 16-59, work in the unorganized sector, and not be an income tax payer or a member of EPFO/ESIC.
insights.quote: If the age of any unorganised worker is between 16-59 years He does not file his income tax return.

insights.takeaway: Self-registration for the e-Shram card requires an Aadhar-linked mobile number, Aadhar card, and bank account details to complete the process online.
insights.quote: You have to keep in mind, that at the time of registration you have to keep your Aadhar no. with you.

insights.takeaway: The e-Shram card provides a Universal Account Number (UAN) and includes a free one-year enrollment in the Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojna (PMSBY) for accident insurance.
insights.quote: For the first year, they will be given a free enrollment of Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojna.

insights.takeaway: If you cannot register online, you can visit a nearby e-Mitra or Common Service Centre (CSC) to get your e-Shram card created with professional assistance.
insights.quote: If you are still finding this process complicated so by going to your nearby e-Mitra or CSC centre.

insights.takeaway: The e-Shram UAN is designed to potentially simplify future transitions into the organized sector, aiming to link worker data directly with PF portals in the future.
insights.quote: If this worker works in the organized sector where the PF is deducted so there, he just needs to give his UAN number.

insights.takeaway: Life insurance is not an investment, it is a protection tool. Its purpose is to secure your family's financial future against uncertain events, not to generate wealth.
insights.quote: Insurance purpose is to protect you and your family from a uncertain event.

insights.takeaway: Never mix insurance and investment. Buying a 'combo' plan often leads to high premiums with poor returns. Keep them separate to maintain flexibility and lower costs.
insights.quote: never mix insurance and investment.

insights.takeaway: Term insurance is the best and cheapest form of life insurance. It provides a high cover for a low premium, allowing you to invest your surplus money elsewhere.
insights.quote: Term Insurance equals to best insurance. Term insurance equals to cheapest Insurance.

insights.takeaway: Calculate your required insurance cover as at least 20 times your annual income. This ensures your family can maintain their lifestyle and beat inflation over time.
insights.quote: the money that you earn in a single year the cover should be 20 times of it.

insights.takeaway: Understand the 'Time Value of Money' before choosing premium payment options. Paying extra for 'Return of Premium' or 'Limited Pay' plans often results in lower overall wealth compared to investing that extra money in mutual funds.
insights.quote: If you are aware, time value will work in your favor. If you are not, it will work in the favor of the company.

insights.takeaway: When comparing insurance companies, look at 'Claim Settlement Ratio by Amount' rather than just the number of claims settled. This provides a more accurate picture of the company's reliability.
insights.quote: Another metric is, claim settlement ratio by amount The reality of the company comes to the fore.

insights.takeaway: Add-on riders like 'Critical Illness' and 'Accidental Disability' are useful, but check if the payout is 'over and above' your base cover or if it reduces your total sum assured.
insights.quote: No one will tell you that, Imagine you had a critical illness and you got 30 lakh rupees. So your 2 crore policy will reduce to 1.7 crore.

insights.takeaway: When interest rates rise on a floating-rate home loan, banks often extend your tenure to keep your EMI constant, which can drastically increase your total interest burden.
insights.quote: The bank has not told you while increasing it. On the 28-year tenure, your EMI will be back to Rs. 25,000.

insights.takeaway: In the early years of a home loan, a large majority of your EMI goes toward interest rather than the principal, meaning your outstanding balance decreases very slowly.
insights.quote: Out of that 5,000 will go to your principal. And 20,000 rupees will go to your interest.

insights.takeaway: Pre-paying your home loan in the early years is the most effective way to save interest because it reduces the principal balance on which future interest is calculated.
insights.quote: Sooner the pre-payment, greater the impact.

insights.takeaway: Paying just one extra EMI per year can significantly reduce your loan tenure and save you lakhs in interest over the life of the loan.
insights.quote: If you pay 13 times a year instead of 12 times, that means, once a year, if you pre-pay additional money equal to 1 EMI, then you will save interest of lakhs.

insights.takeaway: You can claim tax deductions on home loans under Section 80C for principal repayment (up to 1.5 lakhs) and Section 24 for interest payments (up to 2 lakhs).
insights.quote: Section 24 in which you can claim the interest amount towards your home loan which you have paid.

insights.takeaway: Joint home loans allow both co-applicants to claim separate tax deductions for principal and interest, effectively doubling the tax-saving benefit for the household.
insights.quote: Both the people can take all these deductions in their separate ITRs.

insights.takeaway: New RBI rules mandate that banks must provide clear options to borrowers when interest rates change, including the choice to increase EMI instead of tenure to avoid negative amortization.
insights.quote: Banks shall ensure that elongation of tenure in case of floating interest loan does not result in negative amortization.

insights.takeaway: Banks are now required to return property documents within 30 days of full loan repayment, failing which they must pay a penalty of 5,000 rupees per day to the borrower.
insights.quote: As soon as you have fully repaid the loan within the next 30 days the bank will return your property documents to you.

insights.takeaway: Avoid digital gold for long-term investment due to high spreads (3-6%) and lack of regulation. It is often less cost-effective than other gold investment vehicles.
insights.quote: This 3% Spread is not flat. It can easily vary between 3 to 6%.

insights.takeaway: Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGB) are the superior gold investment because they offer 2.5% annual interest, are tax-free upon maturity, and have no storage or making charges.
insights.quote: Its profit in SGB investment is completely tax free.

insights.takeaway: When trading SGBs on the stock exchange, always use limit orders instead of market orders to avoid buying at a premium or selling at a deep discount due to low liquidity.
insights.quote: Always put a limit order so that you will not sold it at 5-10% discount by mistake.

insights.takeaway: Gold ETFs and Gold Mutual Funds are regulated by SEBI, making them safer than digital gold. They are ideal for investment purposes but do not allow for easy physical conversion.
insights.quote: ETFs and Gold mutual funds are regulated by SEBI, so we can confidently say that there is equivalent gold behind our amount.

insights.takeaway: Physical gold jewelry is a poor investment due to high making charges (often 20-30%) and GST, which significantly erode your potential returns compared to bullion or paper gold.
insights.quote: At the price of 89K, I have to pay around 29% Extra Making Charge.

insights.takeaway: SGBs held in a Demat account can be sold on the stock exchange before the 8-year maturity, providing liquidity, though the price will fluctuate based on market demand and supply.
insights.quote: Your SGB price will also depend on demand and supply same as shares.

insights.takeaway: Gold mutual funds hold a small percentage of their assets as cash to manage redemptions, which slightly impacts the total amount of your capital actually invested in gold.
insights.quote: A mutual fund always holds a certain amount as cash.

insights.takeaway: In your 20s, prioritize increasing your active income over long-term investing. Use your savings to acquire high-demand skills or certifications that can 5x or 10x your earning potential.
insights.quote: Your goal should be that... How should you increase your income?

insights.takeaway: Switching jobs strategically is a powerful way to accelerate income growth. Aim to move when you have mastered your current role or when your annual increment is below market standards.
insights.quote: If in that company or in that role, you have nothing to learn, then you must learn about your skill. and by switching... focus towards learning something new.

insights.takeaway: Avoid the 'penny wise, pound foolish' trap. Budgeting is essential; track your Zomato, subscription, and lifestyle expenses to ensure your investment SIPs are significant relative to your income.
insights.quote: These numbers are going to open your eyes.

insights.takeaway: Financial freedom is about creating a second income source or liquid assets that cover your expenses, allowing you to work because you want to, not because you have to.
insights.quote: This is the stage of life, where you can say, By ruining my peace and happiness, I won't only work for money.

insights.takeaway: An emergency fund should be kept in a liquid, safe instrument like a flexible Bank FD. Avoid keeping it in volatile assets like stocks or mutual funds where capital could erode.
insights.quote: The ideal place to park emergency fund is 'Fixed Deposit'. Not all types of FDs. Such FDs which are flexible.

insights.takeaway: Use the 3/20/30/40 rule for home buying: total cost under 3x annual income, tenure under 20 years, total EMIs under 30% of salary, and at least 40% down payment.
insights.quote: This is called 3/20/30/40 formula.

insights.takeaway: Wealth is what you don't see. Avoid buying depreciating assets like new cars just for social status; consider reliable second-hand vehicles to save capital for income-generating investments.
insights.quote: If you are buying too many things, then you'll have a lot of things, not a lot of money.

insights.takeaway: Never purchase property using a General Power of Attorney. It is not a valid ownership document, can be revoked at any time, and is considered illegal for property transfers.
insights.quote: never buy a plot from the power of attorney don't buy yourself

insights.takeaway: Always verify the 'Title Document' of the seller. Ensure the property was acquired legally through a registered sale deed, gift deed, will, or a government conveyance deed.
insights.quote: The most common thing in property law is, that you can give me the title which you already have

insights.takeaway: Obtain an Encumbrance Certificate from the local registrar's office to confirm the property is free from existing loans, mortgages, or third-party legal claims.
insights.quote: he will inform me whether the person took a loan on this property or not?

insights.takeaway: Check the 'Channel Document' history to ensure every previous transfer of the property was legal. A break in the chain of ownership can lead to future litigation.
insights.quote: I have to check that full history The property I am purchasing

insights.takeaway: When buying a flat, always demand the Occupancy Certificate (OC) from the builder. It proves the building complies with municipal regulations and is safe for legal habitation.
insights.quote: if you are buying your bungalow or flat then you must check your builder's OC

insights.takeaway: Request tax receipts and society maintenance NOCs from the seller. These documents prove the seller is the recognized owner and has cleared all financial dues with local authorities.
insights.quote: I check his tax receipt If the government has given him a tax receipt, Meaning that land is in his name only.

insights.takeaway: Verify the land's conversion status before purchase. Buying agricultural land for residential or commercial use without proper government conversion is illegal and can lead to property seizure.
insights.quote: whenever you buy property from someone So check, whether he did a conversion of property or not?

insights.takeaway: Be wary of sellers who pressure you to pay a large token amount quickly. This urgency is often a red flag that the seller is hiding something or is not the rightful owner.
insights.quote: if he is forcing you or compelling you give an advance within 2-3 days So we close it as soon as possible

insights.takeaway: Capital gains are taxed differently based on the asset type and holding period. Equity investments held for over a year are long-term, while debt investments require a three-year holding period.
insights.quote: Short term time frame for DEBT investment is not 1 year but it is 3 years.

insights.takeaway: Intraday trading is not classified as capital gains but as business income, regardless of the holding period, because the intent is to trade rather than hold assets.
insights.quote: If I buy today and sell it today Then this is not considered Capital Gain This is considered as Business Income.

insights.takeaway: You can set off short-term capital losses against short-term capital gains. However, long-term capital losses can only be set off against long-term capital gains.
insights.quote: Short term capital losses can be set off against short term capital gain. Similarly, Long term capital losses can be set off only against long term capital gain.

insights.takeaway: To carry forward capital losses to future years to offset future gains, you must mandatorily file your Income Tax Return (ITR) within the due date.
insights.quote: You have to clearly state it in your income tax return. Then you will be able to forward it.

insights.takeaway: Dividend income is now taxable at your applicable income tax slab rate. Companies may deduct TDS if the annual dividend payout exceeds 5,000 rupees.
insights.quote: Dividend income is considered under income from other sources And you have to pay tax as your slab rates.

insights.takeaway: Use 'Tax Harvesting' to save on LTCG tax. Since the first 1 lakh of long-term capital gains on equity is tax-free, realize these gains annually by selling and repurchasing your holdings.
insights.quote: You should realize your profit of up to 1 lakh after the end of every year.

insights.takeaway: Indexation allows you to adjust the purchase price of assets like debt funds or real estate for inflation, effectively reducing your taxable capital gains.
insights.quote: We will calculate its today's cost which is known as the INDEXED COST.

insights.takeaway: Term insurance is superior to whole life insurance because it provides high coverage at a significantly lower cost, allowing you to invest the surplus money elsewhere for wealth creation.
insights.quote: Whole life insurance is a very illogical thing Its premium is 6-7 times more than TERM insurance

insights.takeaway: When evaluating insurance companies, prioritize the Amount Settlement Ratio over the Claim Settlement Ratio, as the former reflects the actual percentage of money paid out rather than just the number of claims.
insights.quote: Showing a high CSR is very easy for companies They can pass small claims rejecting the big claims

insights.takeaway: Always disclose medical history, smoking, and drinking habits truthfully. Providing incorrect information to lower premiums gives insurance companies a legal basis to reject your family's claims later.
insights.quote: The company can reject your claim if it finds that you gave improper disclosures

insights.takeaway: Avoid ULIPs and Endowment plans for investment purposes. They offer low insurance coverage and poor investment returns that rarely beat inflation, making them inefficient financial products.
insights.quote: These are the worst investment options. Because these are just the opposite of term insurance.

insights.takeaway: Choose a term insurance duration that covers you until your dependents become financially independent, typically around age 65, rather than paying for unnecessary whole-life coverage.
insights.quote: You don't need insurance after the age when no one will be dependent on you

insights.takeaway: Add a Critical Illness rider to your term insurance policy rather than your health insurance. Term insurance premiums are locked for the policy duration, whereas health insurance premiums increase with age.
insights.quote: Term insurance premium will never increase after you once take it But health insurance premium increases with your age

insights.takeaway: Avoid 'Return of Premium' or 'Limited Pay' term insurance options. These plans charge double the premium for benefits that are better achieved by investing your own money in mutual funds or stocks.
insights.quote: Instead, we should invest our extra money to create wealth

insights.takeaway: Avoid taking loans for depreciating assets or lifestyle gadgets like iPhones unless you have guaranteed future cash flow to cover both the principal and interest.
insights.quote: For that, you take loan only when... When you have a guarantee of the future cash flow.

insights.takeaway: Stop relying on your memory for expenses. Track every transaction daily using a diary, app, or template to identify and curb non-essential spending.
insights.quote: Don't trust your mind, but your pen.

insights.takeaway: Eliminate bad habits like smoking or excessive outside eating. Small daily savings, when invested consistently, can grow into significant amounts over time due to compounding.
insights.quote: Because they say 'PItcher is filled drop by drop'. In the same way, the pitcher gets emptied drop by drop too.

insights.takeaway: Maintain a systematic filing system for all financial documents, including insurance policies, warranty cards, and tax records, to avoid late payment penalties and lost claims.
insights.quote: Everything has a designated folder.

insights.takeaway: Focus on product utility rather than brand logos. Your financial status is built through your work and value creation, not by purchasing expensive branded accessories.
insights.quote: You create your own brand.

insights.takeaway: Inflation erodes the value of idle cash. Move savings from low-interest accounts into investment vehicles like Fixed Deposits or other instruments that beat inflation to preserve purchasing power.
insights.quote: The money kept in your locker or bank. It is not safe. The inflation keeps eating it slowly.

insights.takeaway: Reduce monthly household expenses by 10-20% by tracking consumption patterns and purchasing groceries and hygiene products in bulk rather than frequent small quantities.
insights.quote: If with planning All the groceries used in that month. If we buy that in bulk at once. Then, in that, quiet easily. 10 - 20% could be saved.

insights.takeaway: Prioritize physical health as a financial asset. Neglecting health in your youth often leads to significant medical expenses that can deplete your accumulated wealth later in life.
insights.quote: Most people work hard and spend their health... trying to achieve wealth. Then they retire and spend their wealth.. trying to get back their health.

insights.takeaway: Cultivate adaptability by continuously learning new skills. As automation and AI change the job market, the ability to learn and pivot is your greatest financial security.
insights.quote: Hence, it is very important to keep learning. Because, as you keep learning. With that, a very important trait is developed. That is 'Adaptability'.

insights.takeaway: Size your solar system based on your average annual electricity consumption, not just peak summer usage, to ensure maximum financial viability and avoid excess generation that may lapse.
insights.quote: always when we design the solar system So we take the average of the year

insights.takeaway: On-grid solar systems do not require batteries and use the grid as a virtual battery. If the grid power goes out, the solar system automatically shuts down for safety reasons.
insights.quote: when the grid is off, the system automatically shuts down

insights.takeaway: Net metering allows you to export excess electricity generated by your solar system to the grid. You are billed only for the net units consumed after offsetting your production.
insights.quote: this exchange of electricity that you put the electricity in the grid during the day

insights.takeaway: Solar panels degrade by approximately 0.7% annually, but because electricity tariffs typically rise over time, your total financial savings remain consistent or improve over the 25-year lifespan.
insights.quote: performance decreases slightly by 0.7% Your electricity price goes up That's why your savings are constant

insights.takeaway: To ensure a 25-year lifespan, prioritize high-quality, galvanized structures and professional installation. Poor quality structures will rust, compromising the integrity of the entire solar setup.
insights.quote: if your structure is not galvanized in proper zinc not of proper material So your solar structure will start catching rust

insights.takeaway: Dust, soil, and bird droppings can reduce solar panel performance by up to 30%. Regular cleaning with specialized equipment and professional AMC services are essential for efficiency.
insights.quote: If you don't clean your panels for six months supposedly your system's performance will go down up to 30%

insights.takeaway: Government subsidies for residential solar are currently tied to specific 'Made in India' poly-crystalline technology. Always verify local state policies or national portal updates before purchasing.
insights.quote: What subsidy is available in India It is available only on Made in India solar cells and solar panels

insights.takeaway: NPS is a retirement-focused investment system, not just a scheme. It offers a low-cost structure with expense ratios as low as 0.03% to 0.09%, significantly cheaper than most mutual funds.
insights.quote: NPS does not even charge 0.1% as management fees.

insights.takeaway: Under the new tax regime, you can claim a tax deduction for employer contributions to your NPS account under Section 80CCD(2) up to 14% of your basic salary.
insights.quote: if your employer contributes up to 14% of your basic salary in NPS then that whole amount under section 80CCD 2 will be exempted

insights.takeaway: NPS Tier 1 is a mandatory retirement account with tax benefits and lock-in rules, while Tier 2 is a voluntary, flexible investment account with no tax benefits and no lock-in.
insights.quote: the investment made in a Tier 1 account is locked under a lock-in period and you have to follow the rules and regulations to withdraw or exit from it.

insights.takeaway: NPS follows a 'Triple E' tax structure: contributions are deductible, investment growth is tax-free, and the final 60% lump sum withdrawal at age 60 is also tax-free.
insights.quote: NPS is called Triple E Instrument means exempt, exempt, exempt

insights.takeaway: You can automate your NPS investments using the D-REMIT feature, which allows you to set up a virtual ID for systematic contributions similar to a mutual fund SIP.
insights.quote: In which you add a virtual ID to your bank account and through that on a certain date just like you are doing your SIP in mutual funds

insights.takeaway: NPS allows you to choose between 'Auto Choice' (age-based asset allocation) and 'Active Choice' (custom allocation). You can change your asset allocation up to four times per year.
insights.quote: you get the option to change your asset allocation 4 times in a year

insights.takeaway: At age 60, you must use at least 40% of your NPS corpus to purchase an annuity, which provides a lifelong pension. The remaining 60% can be withdrawn as a tax-free lump sum.
insights.quote: 60% of that amount you can withdraw lump sum... the remaining 40% you have to purchase an annuity

insights.takeaway: Medical inflation in India is approximately 14% annually. Without adequate health insurance, a single major hospital bill can wipe out your entire life savings and retirement corpus.
insights.quote: 70-80% of the people in the country Just one hospital bill away from becoming poor.

insights.takeaway: Avoid family floater plans that combine parents with children. Insurers set premiums based on the eldest member's age and health, forcing younger, healthier members to pay higher rates.
insights.quote: make a separate family floater for parents and a separate family floater for you and your spouse

insights.takeaway: Beware of 'sub-limits' on specific treatments like cataract or angioplasty. Even if your total policy cover is high, these hidden caps restrict the maximum payout for common procedures.
insights.quote: the total cover is 50 lakhs but if you come to get a cataract surgery, you will get only 1 lakh.

insights.takeaway: Room rent caps are a major trap. If you exceed the room rent limit, insurers often apply a proportional deduction to your entire hospital bill, not just the room charges.
insights.quote: Majority expenses written in your hospital bill are linked to your room rent cap.

insights.takeaway: Always verify if your policy covers both cashless and reimbursement claims. Some new plans restrict claims to empanelled hospitals only, which is dangerous during emergencies.
insights.quote: if you go to a hospital which is not tied up with them, then you won't get a claim.

insights.takeaway: Never lie about pre-existing diseases when buying insurance. Honesty ensures your claims are not rejected later for non-disclosure, which is a common ground for claim denial.
insights.quote: never lie about your health condition. Whatever disease you have, tell them quietly.

insights.takeaway: Look for policies that offer 'No Claim Bonus' and 'Day Care Treatment' coverage. These features add significant value by increasing your sum assured over time without extra premiums.
insights.quote: Many years are such when you do not even claim from the policy and you get reward for that by increasing your sum assured

insights.takeaway: Use free annual health check-ups provided by your insurer. Maintaining these medical reports helps you prove the absence of pre-existing conditions if a future claim is contested.
insights.quote: by maintaining their files, you will get your claim. Because a lot of claims are rejected.

insights.takeaway: A 1 kW solar system typically generates 1,400 to 1,450 units of electricity annually. Use this ratio to estimate the system size needed based on your total yearly consumption.
insights.quote: If you purchase 1 kW of solar, then consider 1,400 unit yearly.

insights.takeaway: Solar systems are for captive consumption only. The government policy does not encourage oversizing your plant, as excess electricity sold back to the grid fetches a very low price.
insights.quote: It doesn't make any economic sense to sell electricity for Rs 2.5 - 3.

insights.takeaway: On-grid solar systems use net metering, which acts as a free battery by allowing you to export excess daytime power to the grid and draw it back at night.
insights.quote: In a way, the grid is your free of charge battery.

insights.takeaway: On-grid solar systems automatically shut down during power outages for safety reasons, meaning they will not provide power during a grid failure unless paired with a battery.
insights.quote: Once your electricity stops, then your solar's power production also stops.

insights.takeaway: To qualify for government subsidies under the PM Surya Ghar scheme, you must use 'Made in India' solar panels that meet Domestic Content Requirement (DCR) standards.
insights.quote: To avail the advantage of subsidy, India has a rule that your panels must be 'Made in India'.

insights.takeaway: String inverters are the most cost-effective choice for 95% of homes, but optimizers or microinverters are better if your roof faces significant shading issues.
insights.quote: 90% - 95% customers prefer String Inverter, which is the most cost-efficient technology.

insights.takeaway: Poor maintenance can cause solar systems to underperform by 30-40%. Budget for professional maintenance to ensure you hit your projected ROI and electricity savings.
insights.quote: It was found that 50% residential solar that was installed. There are underperformance issues in more than 30%.

insights.takeaway: Under Section 45 of the Insurance Act, an insurer cannot reject a life insurance claim on any grounds, including fraud, after the policy has been in force for three years.
insights.quote: After completion of 3 years, Even If the company found any fraud done by you The company has no right to reject your claim

insights.takeaway: Avoid 'Limited Pay' and 'Return of Premium' term insurance plans. They are mathematically inferior to 'Regular Pay' plans combined with disciplined SIP investments for wealth creation.
insights.quote: You are offering the magic of the power of compounding to someone else in Limited Pay

insights.takeaway: Do not over-rely on the 'Sovereign Guarantee' of LIC. In a catastrophic scenario where a massive insurer fails, the government's ability to honor claims is practically questionable.
insights.quote: The government may guarantee it but the government can't honor it practically

insights.takeaway: Online term insurance policies are as valid as those bought through agents. If a claim is rejected solely due to the purchase method, you can legally challenge the insurer using Section 45.
insights.quote: It doesn't matter for a company that you take a policy from an agent or you opt online policy

insights.takeaway: Total life insurance coverage across all your policies should not exceed 25 times your annual income, as insurers will not pay out claims beyond the assessed financial loss.
insights.quote: all your life insurances or term plans combinedly should not be more than 25X of your income.

insights.takeaway: Maintain accurate health records and consider periodic full-body checkups. Having documented proof of your health status over time helps prevent claim delays or rejections.
insights.quote: You should do your full body medical checkup every 6 months to 1 year. And save that report online and physically also

insights.takeaway: If you are a smoker, you must disclose it accurately. If you quit smoking for at least 12 continuous months, you may be eligible for a revision of your premium to non-smoker rates.
insights.quote: If you don't smoke continuously for 12 months then you will be considered a non-smoker

insights.takeaway: Credit cards are only for those who do not need them. If you cannot afford an item with your own money, you have no right to purchase it using bank funds.
insights.quote: Credit cards are for those who do not need them.

insights.takeaway: Paying only the minimum amount due on a credit card is a trap. It causes you to lose your interest-free period and triggers high interest rates of 40% to 50% per annum.
insights.quote: You lost your interest-free period as soon as you paid your minimum payment.

insights.takeaway: No-cost EMIs are not interest-free loans. They are marketing tactics where the interest cost is hidden in the product price, encouraging you to spend more than you originally planned.
insights.quote: This is not an interest-free loan. In fact, as per RBI's circular, it's not allowed to offer interest free loan.

insights.takeaway: Maintain a Credit Utilization Ratio of 30% to 40% of your total limit. Maxing out your credit limit signals to bureaus that you are credit-hungry, which can lower your CIBIL score.
insights.quote: Always spend 30% to 40% of your allowed credit limit.. Not more.

insights.takeaway: To avoid overspending with a credit card, treat it like a prepaid card. Calculate your monthly expenses and pay that amount to your credit card company in advance.
insights.quote: Why don't you convert your credit card into a debit card?

insights.takeaway: Only choose credit cards that offer rewards on expenses you would have incurred anyway. Do not increase your spending just to chase reward points, as the cost of extra spending outweighs the benefits.
insights.quote: Only purchase those items which you would have purchased even if you didn't have a credit card.

insights.takeaway: Legitimate companies never ask you to pay money to start a job. If a company demands fees for 'utility', 'maintenance', or 'registration', it is a scam.
insights.quote: The company never asks for money from you.

insights.takeaway: Be wary of 'work from home' offers that promise high payouts for simple tasks like captcha filling or typing. These are designed to trap you into paying fake penalties.
insights.quote: Earn Rs 30,000 from home without a computer in only 10 days

insights.takeaway: Fraudulent companies use fake legal threats and impersonate court officials to extort money. Real legal notices are sent via formal channels, not by random callers demanding instant payments.
insights.quote: They call you on behalf of the Court. They say that they are calling from Delhi Court.

insights.takeaway: A valid contract requires proper notarization, signatures from both parties, and witnesses. Agreements lacking these are legally weak and often used by scammers to intimidate victims.
insights.quote: If you see in this, it is just a picture of the sign and not a real sign.

insights.takeaway: If a company has an 'intent to cheat' from the start, such as not verifying your qualifications or bank details, you can file a complaint under Section 420 of the IPC.
insights.quote: We can file a case against this company under Section 420. Because this is Intent to Cheat.

insights.takeaway: If you are being blackmailed by a fake company, record all calls and collect evidence. Inconsistent stories from callers are proof of their fraudulent intent.
insights.quote: To prove their Intent to Cheat, if you record the calls, you will realize that they said different conditions.

insights.takeaway: Check online consumer complaint forums before engaging with unknown companies. If many people report the same 'pay-to-work' scam, it is a clear red flag to avoid them.
insights.quote: If we search OVAL SOLUTIONS & UNITEC SOLUTIONS on Google, the first result will be Consumer Complaints.

insights.takeaway: The new tax regime now offers a zero-tax liability for individuals with an annual income up to 12 lakhs, thanks to revised tax slabs and an increased Section 87A rebate of 60,000.
insights.quote: NO INCOME TAX PAYABLE UP TO INCOME OF 12 LAKH RUPEES

insights.takeaway: Salaried employees can effectively earn up to 12.75 lakhs without paying income tax, as the 12 lakh rebate limit is combined with the standard deduction of 75,000.
insights.quote: For a salaried employee, For income up to 12.75 lakhs, no tax will be levied.

insights.takeaway: The government has increased the MSME classification limits, raising the investment threshold to 1.5 crores and the turnover limit to 10 crores, allowing more businesses to access government benefits.
insights.quote: The initial investment criteria has been increased 1.5 times. And the turnover criteria has been doubled.

insights.takeaway: The TDS threshold for professional service payments has been increased from 30,000 to 50,000, and the limit for bank interest TDS for senior citizens has doubled to 1 lakh.
insights.quote: For the senior citizens, the current bank interest they receive... limit has been increased to 1 lakh.

insights.takeaway: Homeowners can now own two self-occupied houses without adding notional rent to their taxable income, significantly reducing the tax burden for those with multiple properties.
insights.quote: If you have 2 self-occupied houses, then you don't have to add the notional rent to your income.

insights.takeaway: The time limit to revise your Income Tax Return (ITR) has been extended from 2 years to 4 years, providing taxpayers more flexibility to correct past filings.
insights.quote: Earlier, the limit was 2 years, and now it has been increased to 4 years.

insights.takeaway: Startups registered before April 1, 2030, remain eligible for government tax relief and benefits, and the credit guarantee limit for startups has been increased to 20 crores.
insights.quote: The government has extended the incorporation date to... before 1st April, 2030.

insights.takeaway: Purchase term and health insurance early to lock in lower premiums, as rates increase with age and health conditions, and ensure you have adequate coverage for financial security.
insights.quote: The earlier you purchase a term insurance, the better... Because, it's premium which is set once.

insights.takeaway: The government introduced three new EPFO-linked employment schemes, including salary subsidies for freshers in manufacturing and non-manufacturing sectors to boost job creation.
insights.quote: Three schemes have been designed around EPFO.

insights.takeaway: A new internship scheme aims to provide 1 crore youth with internships in top 500 companies, with the government covering stipends of up to INR 5,000 per month.
insights.quote: 1 crore youth will be offered internships in top 500 companies.

insights.takeaway: Students pursuing higher education in India can now access collateral-free loans up to INR 10 Lakhs, supported by an e-voucher system providing a 3% interest subvention.
insights.quote: Government will provide assistance to opt for collateral-free loan of up to INR 10L.

insights.takeaway: NPS Vatsalya allows parents to invest in a pension account for their minor children, which converts to a standard NPS account once the child reaches 18 years of age.
insights.quote: In NPS Vatsalya, parents can invest against their minor child.

insights.takeaway: Short-term capital gains tax on equity and mutual funds has increased from 15% to 20%, while long-term capital gains tax has risen from 10% to 12.5%.
insights.quote: In the current budget, the government has increased it from 15% to 20%.

insights.takeaway: Real estate long-term capital gains tax is now 12.5% without indexation benefits, which may increase the tax liability for those selling properties held for a long duration.
insights.quote: Because, properties were sold after 5, 10, 15 or 20 years. So a huge benefit of indexation was offered. But, that has been removed.

insights.takeaway: Securities Transaction Tax (STT) on Futures and Options (F&O) has been increased by 1.5 times, significantly raising the cost of trading for active market participants.
insights.quote: STT (Securities Transaction Tax) on Future's and Options compared to earlier, has now been increased 1.5 times.

insights.takeaway: The new tax regime now offers a higher standard deduction of INR 75,000 for salaried employees, resulting in potential tax savings of up to INR 17,500 for certain income brackets.
insights.quote: The standard deduction that the salaried employees used to receive of INR 50,000... has now been increased to INR 75,000.

insights.takeaway: With healthcare inflation rising at approximately 14% annually, it is essential to secure comprehensive health insurance and term insurance early to lock in lower premiums for life.
insights.quote: If you take Term Insurance at an early age... your premium will be INR 5,000 lifetime.

insights.takeaway: The new labour codes mandate that basic salary must constitute at least 50% of your total CTC. This change directly impacts calculations for PF, gratuity, and other statutory benefits.
insights.quote: A minimum of 50% of the total calculated salary, you will receive that as a basic salary.

insights.takeaway: Under the new codes, all employees, regardless of salary level, must receive their monthly wages by the 7th of the following month. This rule is now universally applicable.
insights.quote: It's clearly stated in the new code, that 'salaries must be paid by 7th of next month'.

insights.takeaway: Fixed-term employees are now legally entitled to gratuity if their contract duration is one year or more, calculated on a pro-rata basis.
insights.quote: Any fixed-term employment whose duration is one year or more. It is mandatory to offer gratuity in such cases.

insights.takeaway: Full and final settlement for resigned or terminated employees must be processed by the employer within two days, while gratuity payments must be completed within 30 days.
insights.quote: The employer has to process the full and final settlement within two days.

insights.takeaway: Gig and platform workers are now brought under the social security ambit, with aggregators required to contribute 1% to 2% of their annual turnover to a universal social security fund.
insights.quote: These platforms have to provide 1% to 2% of their annual turnover to the government.

insights.takeaway: Employers are now legally required to provide an appointment letter to every employee. Failure to provide proper documentation or wage slips can lead to penalties.
insights.quote: It has become mandatory in these codes, If you hire an employee, then it's mandatory to provide an appointment letter.

insights.takeaway: The threshold for requiring government approval for factory closures or layoffs has been increased from 100 to 300 employees, reducing compliance burdens for most MSMEs.
insights.quote: But this limit has now been increased to 300.

insights.takeaway: Women are now permitted to work night shifts in factories, provided they give their consent. Employers are advised to obtain this consent in writing.
insights.quote: They have now been allowed in night shifts too. Although, with consent.

insights.takeaway: Proprietorships require no formal registration to start, making them the simplest entity. However, they offer no separation between personal and business assets, meaning you are personally liable for all business debts.
insights.quote: There is no need of registration in this. There is no other issue or compliance.

insights.takeaway: Avoid registering for GST solely to open a business bank account. Wait until your turnover approaches the mandatory threshold of 40 lakhs to avoid unnecessary compliance costs and tax headaches.
insights.quote: You must not do this, Why? I will explain it to you by the end of this video.

insights.takeaway: In Private Limited companies, LLPs, and OPCs, your liability is limited to the company's assets. Personal assets like your house or car are generally protected from business loan recovery.
insights.quote: In the case of these companies and entities, the liability of a partner or a director is limited.

insights.takeaway: If you are starting a startup with co-founders, consider a partnership firm initially. It has fewer compliance requirements than a Private Limited company and can be converted later once the business scales.
insights.quote: Instead of forming a Private Ltd, you can form a Partnership firm. The compliances will be lesser in that firm.

insights.takeaway: Register a Private Limited company only if you require external funding, plan to issue ESOPs, or need to build trust with large corporate clients who prefer dealing with formal entities.
insights.quote: Only those people must register Private Limited... who are operating huge and highly risky ventures.

insights.takeaway: The Hindu Undivided Family (HUF) is a unique tax-saving entity for Hindu, Sikh, Jain, and Buddhist families. It is treated as a separate tax entity with its own income tax slab and exemptions.
insights.quote: For HUF, for all tax purposes, is treated as a different person.

insights.takeaway: Use a screener to filter mutual funds by category, removing debt and hybrid options. Focus on long-term metrics like 5-year and 10-year CAGR to evaluate performance effectively.
insights.quote: In any category where there could be 50 to 100 Mutual Funds. How should you find Top 3?

insights.takeaway: Rolling returns are a superior metric for consistency compared to point-to-point returns, as they average performance across various market cycles rather than just two specific dates.
insights.quote: 3 Year Average Annual Rolling Return means.. One return will be retrieved from 2013 to 2016.

insights.takeaway: The Sharpe Ratio measures risk-adjusted returns. A higher ratio is better, as it indicates the fund generates more return for every unit of risk taken. Reject funds with negative Sharpe ratios.
insights.quote: It means more the Sharpe ratio the better. Because it'll state If the mutual fund has taken risk, it should provide extra returns.

insights.takeaway: Always check the fund manager's tenure. If a manager changes, the fund's investment style, risk profile, and future performance metrics may shift significantly, rendering past data less relevant.
insights.quote: If the manager has changed.. then all these numbers were derived by the previous manager.

insights.takeaway: Portfolio composition is critical. Check the P/E and P/B ratios and ensure the fund is not overly concentrated in the top 10 holdings to avoid excessive sector-specific risk.
insights.quote: Composition means the funds in which the companies have invested. whether they are well diversified or not.

insights.takeaway: Avoid the mistake of chasing the #1 ranked fund every year. Frequent switching triggers exit loads and capital gains taxes, which destroy the power of compounding over the long term.
insights.quote: Never chase the first rank fund every year. Every mutual fund can't stay on the 1st rank every year.

insights.takeaway: When comparing funds with similar returns, use the Expense Ratio as a tie-breaker. Lower expense ratios mean more of the fund's returns stay in your pocket rather than going to management fees.
insights.quote: You can in fact add another filtter on the screener, i.e. 'Expense Ratio'. and you can sort the funds accordingly.

insights.takeaway: Avoid health insurance policies offered by specific hospitals. These create a conflict of interest where the hospital acts as both provider and insurer, potentially limiting your treatment options and rights.
insights.quote: Your coverage becomes your prison.

insights.takeaway: Always prioritize increasing your total sum insured over reducing your premium. Aim for a higher coverage amount (e.g., 30-40 lakhs) rather than settling for a lower cover to save on premiums.
insights.quote: You need to focus on increasing the cover, rather than decreasing the premium.

insights.takeaway: Check your policy for 'Room Rent Limits'. If you exceed this limit, insurers often apply a proportionate deduction, forcing you to pay a significant percentage of the entire hospital bill yourself.
insights.quote: Not only will you have to pay the extra room rent. But you will also have to pay 50% of your hospital bill from your end.

insights.takeaway: Ensure your health insurance policy does not have 'Disease-wise Sub-limits'. These clauses cap the payout for specific treatments, effectively making a large policy useless for common medical procedures.
insights.quote: Make sure that you don't have a disease sub limit in your policy.

insights.takeaway: Avoid policies with 'Co-pay' clauses, which require you to pay a percentage of every hospital bill out of your own pocket, regardless of your total sum insured.
insights.quote: This is very dangerous and make sure it's not included in your policy.

insights.takeaway: Look for a 'Restoration Benefit' in your policy that triggers from the second claim onwards and allows the same patient to use it for the same illness if the base sum is exhausted.
insights.quote: A truly useful restoration is the one.. which will help you use the restoration from the second claim onwards.

insights.takeaway: Prioritize policies that offer a 'Renewal Bonus' (or No Claim Bonus) that increases your coverage annually, even if you have made a claim in the previous year.
insights.quote: Even if you claim it, you will receive a bonus next year.

insights.takeaway: Monetize your hobbies like art and craft by creating handmade items such as envelopes or soft toys, then marketing them on social media to find local buyers.
insights.quote: anything made by hand, has a great demand, you can make it in some quantity, and share it on social media

insights.takeaway: Utilize empty rooms in your home as a bed and breakfast service for students or tourists by listing your space on platforms like Airbnb, Goibibo, or MakeMyTrip.
insights.quote: you feel that now you have grown-up children, a room is left empty, a guest room is left empty, we can give it on rent

insights.takeaway: Offer professional babysitting services in your neighborhood by creating a safe, designated space for children and marketing your availability through social media or local pamphlets.
insights.quote: you know how to take good care of the baby, so you can also offer this in your spare time

insights.takeaway: Start a professional home-based cleaning service, especially during festive seasons like Diwali, by offering deep cleaning for homes and offices using your own equipment.
insights.quote: this work, we can start in our colony. You can also start this, on a small scale you can also keep a helper with you.

insights.takeaway: Provide premium laundry and ironing services for corporate employees who prefer better care for their clothes than what is typically offered by roadside vendors.
insights.quote: women can do this work well. And can be done with their household chores in many corporate offices the singles they want their clothes to be washed well.

insights.takeaway: Offer gift wrapping and wedding packing services by partnering with local wholesalers or gift shops to provide decorative packaging for corporate clients and events.
insights.quote: if you have this skill you can wrap the gift well and you can do it in a traditional way or in a decorative way

insights.takeaway: Leverage your existing skills in beauty, yoga, or hairdressing to offer home-based professional services, allowing you to earn income while maintaining a flexible schedule.
insights.quote: That skill of yours which has been suppressed by the burden of household whether you can do yoga, or you can do beautician work
